name: ExRAP (Exploratory Retrieval-Augmented Planning)
venue: NeurIPS 2024 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, pp. 67034-67060). arXiv:2509.08222 posted 2025-09-10 is a later mirror of the same paper.
authors_affiliation: Minjong Yoo, Jinwoo Jang, Honguk Woo (Dept. of Computer Science and Engineering, Sungkyunkwan University); Wei-jin Park (Acryl Inc.). Corresponding author: Honguk Woo.
task_domain: Embodied instruction following / LLM-based task planning for embodied agents (home robotics in VirtualHome and ALFRED, skill-based autonomous driving in CARLA).
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent embodied planning in dynamic, non-stationary environments. Introduces 'continual instruction following': a set of M conditional instructions (e.g. 'If the temperature is high, open the window') that are conducted continuously and simultaneously, where conditions may become satisfied/unsatisfied over time, requiring ongoing environment exploration. No agent fine-tuning is performed; planning uses a frozen LLM (LLaMA-3-8B default) with in-context learning. An expert planning demonstration dataset D_e is assumed available for in-context exploitation-value estimation. Objective combines task success rate (SR) and average pending step (PS).
what_is_retrieved: Two retrieval targets: (1) environmental-context quadruples (se, re, te, t) from a temporal embodied knowledge graph (TEKG) accumulated from agent observations, retrieved for query evaluation; (2) expert planning demonstrations from an offline dataset D_e, retrieved by graph similarity to the current observation for exploitation-value (skill-value) estimation.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID. The TEKG environmental-context memory is a GROWING/episodic store the agent writes online from observations; the expert demonstration dataset D_e for in-context skill-value estimation is a STATIC external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k retrieval for both stores: k=12 quadruples per query and 3 demonstrations per instruction are retrieved via similarity sampling/ranking. There is no completeness or precision-driven variable-size objective; selection of which executions to act on is governed by a probability threshold theta=0.5 on query satisfaction rather than a retrieval-completeness criterion.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve] (partial) - retrieves demonstrations and memory quadruples; no Reuse/Revise/Retain of solution cases in the CBR sense. Not a case-based-reasoning method. [uncertain] as a CBR mapping.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for embodied planning and never invokes case-based reasoning or cites Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: (1) (source-entity, relation, target-entity, timestep) quadruple from the temporal embodied knowledge graph (a (state) tuple / KG-subgraph unit); (2) full expert planning demonstration (trajectory) for in-context skill valuation.
index_source: Hybrid: the TEKG environmental-context memory is online/test-time-induced (built and updated from streaming observations during deployment); the expert demonstration dataset D_e is an offline static corpus (100 trajectories across 10 settings in VirtualHome, 50 trajectories each in ALFRED and CARLA).
index_structure_topology: Dependency/knowledge GRAPH: the environmental context memory is a temporal embodied knowledge graph (TEKG) of timestamped quadruples representing objects, relations, states, and room adjacencies. Retrieval over the graph is performed via sentence-embedding similarity (effectively a flat similarity index over quadruples linearized as text). The demonstration store is similarity-keyed by observation graph.
retriever_type: Dense/hybrid. Quadruple and demonstration retrieval uses sentence-embedding similarity (DPR: dpr-ctx_encoder-single-nq-base) combined with BM25 for in-context example retrieval. Quadruple sampling uses a multinomial softmax over highest sentence-embedding similarity between a quadruple and any task directive.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). Retrievers are pre-trained/frozen (DPR + BM25); no retriever training, contrastive fine-tuning, LM-feedback, or RL signal is applied to the retriever itself.
query_construction: Instructions are decomposed by an LLM-based instruction interpreter Phi_I into queries Q (conditions to be checked, e.g. 'TV is off') and executions E (manipulations), with a conditional function C mapping each query to its execution. Queries and executions then serve as the retrieval keys against the TEKG and demonstration store.
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/state-level. Instruction decomposition into query/execution is task-level (done once via Phi_I), but query evaluation against the memory and skill-value-based retrieval are re-run at every timestep (step-level) as the memory and observations change.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / per-step. At each timestep the agent re-evaluates queries against memory (retrieving fresh quadruples) and retrieves demonstrations for skill-value estimation; retrieval is woven into the per-step planning loop (Algorithm 1).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (per-timestep loop). Query re-evaluation by the LLM is additionally gated by a change detector: if the retrieved subgraph is unchanged (G_hat_{1:t} == G_hat_{1:t-1}) the prior response R(q|G_{t-1}) is reused, otherwise the LLM re-evaluates - an efficiency-driven staleness/change trigger rather than a confidence-based one.
reranking: No explicit learned reranking stage. Quadruples are sampled by a multinomial softmax over embedding similarity; in-context examples use DPR + BM25 scoring. Temporal-consistency refinement filters (not reranks) query-response priors by an entropy-monotonicity constraint.
retrieved_context_refinement: Distractor/staleness filtering via temporal-consistency refinement: multiple query-response priors are sampled (10 iterations) using the LLM over retrieved memory, and any response whose entropy does not increase relative to the previous step (violating the information-decay constraint H(R(q|G_{t-1})) > H(P(q|G_{t-1}))) is discarded; surviving responses are averaged. Memory update function mu also removes semantically contradictory/outdated quadruples.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation. Retrieved quadruples plus demonstrations are linearized into the LLM prompt: (a) for memory-augmented probabilistic query evaluation Phi_M estimating P(q|G_t), and (b) for in-context exploitation skill-value estimation v_T. Retrieval is not used as a training signal.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved, retrieve-then-plan within a continuous loop. Each step: (a) evaluate queries via retrieved memory to select active executions E_t (threshold theta=0.5); (b) score each candidate skill z by a weighted sum of an LLM-derived exploitation value v_T (using retrieved demonstrations + memory) and an information-gain exploration value v_R, then execute argmax skill; update memory; repeat.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call / per-skill within the rollout: retrieval and value estimation are performed for every skill-selection step in the continual loop, and per-query for the evaluation stage.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR/case-adaptation method). Retrieved demonstrations are used as verbatim in-context exemplars to estimate exploitation skill value rather than adapted into a new plan.
retrieved_item_representation: Structured note / linearized knowledge-graph text: retrieved TEKG quadruples are injected as linearized relational facts (e.g. '(TV, is, off, 27)'); demonstrations are injected as raw in-context trajectory exemplars.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Low-level/raw: timestamped state quadruples (raw environmental facts) and raw demonstration trajectories; no distilled strategy, guideline, or reusable workflow abstraction.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Entropy-based temporal-consistency refinement on query evaluation (discards stale/inconsistent LLM responses whose entropy fails to grow with time, modeling information decay) and a memory update function mu that removes contradictory and outdated quadruples (e.g. conflicting object states/positions). No retriever-aware training or distractor-aware SFT.
memory_type: Graph + episodic: a temporal embodied knowledge graph (TEKG) of timestamped quadruples serving as the environmental-context memory, accumulated episodically from observations.
write_back: True. Each observation o_{t+1} is integrated into the memory via update function mu (G_{t+1} = mu(G_t, o_{t+1})), which adds new quadruples and removes contradicting/outdated ones.
online_growth: Yes. The TEKG environmental-context memory grows and is continuously synchronized during deployment as the agent observes the changing environment. (The offline expert demonstration store D_e is frozen.)
write_back_trigger: Per-step: memory is updated at every timestep from the new observation produced by executing the selected skill (Algorithm 1 line: G_{t+1} = mu(G_t, o_{t+1})). Writes are observation-driven, not success/failure- or reflection-gated.
failure_experience_usage: Not used. Memory stores environmental-state observations, not success/failure planning outcomes; there is no storage or contrastive retrieval of failed planning experiences. (Baseline LLM-Planner uses execution-error feedback, but ExRAP's memory does not store failure cases.)
memory_evolution_update: Dedup-merge + forget/overwrite: the update function mu retains only most-recent quadruples for agent-related entities and removes semantically contradictory or outdated quadruples (opposite object states, or an object in two places), effectively delta-updating and pruning stale facts.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/selection is fixed similarity top-k (DPR/BM25 + softmax sampling); it is not a learned or RL-optimized retrieval policy. The exploration value uses an information-gain (mutual-information difference) estimate, but this scores skills, not the retriever.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private environmental-context memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: VirtualHome (household, 19 continual instructions, 162 object types), ALFRED (household vision-and-language, 16 continual instructions, 58 object types / 26 receptacles / 120 scenes), CARLA (skill-based autonomous driving, 16 continual instructions). Non-stationarity levels: low/medium/high (condition changes every 8/6/4 timesteps). Instruction scales: 3/5/7. Instruction types: sentence-wise, summarized, object-ambiguation.
benchmark_family: Embodied (ALFRED, VirtualHome) + embodied autonomous-driving simulator (CARLA). Adapted to a novel 'continual instruction following' protocol with controlled non-stationarity.
baselines: ZSP (Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners, Huang et al. 2022), SayCan (Brohan et al. 2023, with optimal per-environment affordance function), ProgPrompt (Singh et al. 2023, VirtualHome/ALFRED only), LLM-Planner (Song et al. 2023, implemented as a step-wise variant; most competitive baseline).
key_metrics: Task Success Rate SR (higher is better; proportion of completed tasks whose conditions are satisfied) and Pending Step PS (lower is better; average timesteps to complete a task after its condition is actually satisfied).
headline_result: Under medium non-stationarity in VirtualHome, ExRAP reaches SR 55.14% / PS 11.33 vs LLM-Planner 39.89% / 15.93. Averaged across non-stationarity levels and environments, ExRAP improves SR by ~16.45% and reduces PS by ~3.40 over the strongest baseline (LLM-Planner); best single point e.g. ALFRED low non-stationarity SR 69.90%.
ablations: Temporal consistency (ExRAP-TC, removes temporal-consistency refinement): ExRAP outperforms it by ~15.56% SR on average. Exploration strategy: vs ExRAP-LLM (LLM-prompted 'explore the home' instead of information-based exploration) and ExRAP-EXP (exploitation-only planner with 'Find {query}' commands), ExRAP is higher by ~26.76% and ~17.46% on average respectively. LLM scale (Table 6): ExRAP stays robust with small Gemma-2B (SR 52.75%) while LLM-Planner/SayCan degrade sharply, also tested with Llama-3-8B (default) and Llama-3-70B. Computation overhead (Table A.8): retrieval+inference ~14x faster than no-retrieval LLM inference (2.203s vs 31.243s).
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (SR, PS) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are decoupled or reported.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both outcome and process: SR is outcome; PS is a process/efficiency metric (latency to act after condition satisfaction). Additional qualitative process analyses include exploration heatmaps, exploration-value dynamics, temporal-consistency refinement examples, and mapping of ExRAP's behavior to Greedy / Multiple-Instruction-First / Max-Staleness-First heuristics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported: retrieval is cheap (quadruple retrieval 0.021s, demonstration retrieval 0.024s) and retrieval-augmented LLM inference is 2.203s vs 31.243s without retrieval (~14x speedup) by capping context to 3 demonstrations + 12 quadruples regardless of graph/dataset size. Each experiment run ~4 hours on 2x RTX A6000. Query evaluation samples 10 LLM iterations per query, which the paper notes increases compute relative to baselines (a stated limitation).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k, budget-capped: k=12 retrieved quadruples per query and 3 demonstrations per continual instruction; number of prompts=3; max new tokens=40; query-evaluator iterations=10; execution-selection threshold theta=0.5. Retrieval count is held constant regardless of memory size to bound context length.
builds_on: RAG for LLMs (REPLUG, Self-RAG, Active RAG, Chain-of-Note); LLM-Planner (RAG with task-specific demonstrations for embodied planning); DREAM (Liu et al. 2021, mutual-information-based decoupled exploration in meta-RL, adapted here for exploration-value estimation); SayCan / ProgPrompt / ZSP (LLM embodied planners); continuous-queries database literature (Liu 1999, Watanabe 2010).
contrasts_with: Instruction-wise / single in-situ LLM planners (ZSP, SayCan, ProgPrompt, LLM-Planner) that plan one isolated instruction at a time, re-collect environment knowledge each plan, and do not handle continual/simultaneous instructions or non-stationarity; standard RAG that retrieves static demonstrations without continuously synchronizing an environmental memory or integrating exploration.
lineage: Group C (retrieval-augmented planning). Positioned in the embodied LLM-planning lineage that extends RAG with a growing, exploration-driven environmental-context memory: it advances from demonstration-retrieval planners (LLM-Planner) toward dynamic memory-grounded continual planning, uniquely fusing information-based exploration with retrieval-augmented LLM planning.
code_url: [uncertain] No official ExRAP code repository was located via arXiv, the NeurIPS poster page, OpenReview, or web/GitHub search (GitHub 'rap' results are unrelated works). Likely none publicly released.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill-description retrieval; skills are a fixed primitive action set per environment).
index_content_separation: Partial: a lightweight similarity index over linearized quadruples retrieves only 12 quadruples on demand from a potentially large TEKG, separating the heavy full graph from the small injected context, but not a formal SOP-index-then-content scheme.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool API store; skills are environment-native primitives such as walk/grab/switch/open/close, goto/toggle, turn/go-straight/load-offload).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (see CBR fields; demonstrations used as verbatim in-context exemplars, not adapted cases).
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (primary method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A as a standalone benchmark contribution, but the paper constructs a continual-instruction-following protocol: 19 (VirtualHome) / 16 (ALFRED) / 16 (CARLA) hand-written conditional instructions, evaluated over low/medium/high non-stationarity (condition change every 8/6/4 steps), instruction scales 3/5/7, and three instruction types; 95% CIs over 10 seeds (VirtualHome) and 5 seeds (ALFRED, CARLA).
